instruction: Find the highest revenue value in column G and highlight that cell with a background color.

metadata.explanation: Task requires finding and highlighting the maximum revenue. Verified with Python: max revenue is 479.13 at cell G26 (row 26). Evaluator checks if G26 has background fill color applied.

llm_judge_reasons: Critical incomplete verification: Evaluator only checks if cell G26 has a background fill, but does NOT verify that G26 actually contains the highest revenue value in column G
The instruction has TWO requirements: (1) find the highest revenue value, (2) highlight that cell. The evaluator only checks requirement (2) for a hardcoded cell
If user highlights the wrong cell (e.g., any cell other than the actual maximum), the evaluator will incorrectly fail even if that cell has correct highlighting
Conversely, the evaluator cannot detect if the user highlights G26 when the actual maximum is in a different cell (if data changes)
The evaluator assumes G26 contains the maximum based on metadata, but doesn't verify this assumption at runtime
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: The getter should scan column G to find which cell(s) have background fill applied, not hardcode cell G26
The metric should verify: (a) exactly one cell in column G has highlighting, (b) that highlighted cell contains the maximum value in column G
Alternative approach: getter extracts all values from column G and identifies which cells are highlighted, then metric verifies the highlighted cell matches the max value location
Remove hardcoded cell 'G26' from result config - the evaluator should dynamically find highlighted cells
